endings.title: Half the story
epilogue: The owners' audit found the 118 unexplained entries in your own review, the one the board never saw.
You resigned before the chair could ask. The lock standard you wrote was adopted anyway, under someone else's name.
Lesson: a board can forgive bad news. It never forgives being kept from it.

endings.title: The inquiry
epilogue: Maren Varnham learned the truth from a reporter, and the inquiry that followed was about Veldane's silence more than the intruder.
Counsel kept the company's liability small. The reputation never recovered, and nor did yours.
Lesson: candour and legal care fit together. Silence fits with neither.

endings.title: The record that wasn't
epilogue: Years later a lawyer asked for the original patrol logs, and the ones on file didn't match the clock.
Everything you built after that was read in its light. You left the industry quietly.
Lesson: a record is only worth something if nobody has ever changed it.

endings.title: The form
epilogue: When the big claim came, Tarrowby went back to the renewal form and found the claim that had been left off it.
Cover was disputed, the owners paid, and the board asked who signed the form.
Lesson: an insurer prices what it is told. Tell it everything.

endings.title: Running on empty
epilogue: You reached the top with nothing left. Six months into the job your doctor signed you off, and the deputy you never had time to train ran the programme alone.
Lesson: crisis leaders rest between crises, or they stop being leaders.

endings.title: The one that got away
epilogue: The board funded the programme and the buyer went to prison. But the cards that opened room 907 came from stock taken by a man you once warned off before the police could act.
You still think about the phone call.
Lesson: leave the arrest to the police. A warning only moves the problem.

endings.title: The Veldane standard
epilogue: A year after room 907, you went back to the board with the number. Unexplained entries were down by two thirds across the group, and every one had been investigated.
The night officer you trained on your first shift runs the Harbourfront now. Other companies borrow your field manual; you let them.
Lesson: observe, report, de-escalate, and tell the truth. It scales.

endings.title: The people's VP
epilogue: Staff across the group knew your name and trusted that a report to you would be heard. Some of the numbers lagged, but the people who would fix them stayed.
Lesson: a programme is only as good as the people who speak up in it.

endings.title: The numbers person
epilogue: Insurers cut the group's premium and owners funded every case you made. Some floors still felt the strain of the changes, and you knew it.
Lesson: the numbers win the budget. The people make it work.

endings.title: Safe hands
epilogue: Nothing about your tenure made the news, which in this job is the point. The programme was sound, if not yet loved.
Lesson: safe is the start. The best programmes are trusted too.

endings.title: Unfinished business
epilogue: Your career came to a pause before the work was done. The field manual you kept is still in the drawer of the LP office, and the night shift still reads it.
Lesson: every case is a chance to try again, and to do it by the book.
